- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to reflect risk-off bias.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >3x historical mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias of 10–20% for next 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >2.5σ above mean, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in 3 consecutive days triggers “sentiment shock” — model overreacts; dampen forecast by 20–40% for next 7 days.
- If forecast is >1.5x true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model is “overconfident” — reduce by 10–25% unless sentiment is strong and rising.
